status: the release pin since 2026-10-19 (tools/xp_csmwrap_esp.sh PINNED, release.go, lock.json; X470 Windows Me PASS with the in-place kit me-usb2, docs/research/csmwrap.md section 23). The csmwrap.ini options are unchanged; 0022 adds stage 2 (hot-swap) of the USB disk service, active only with int13_boot_disk_only = true (the Windows 9x flow), docs/usb9x-hotswap-design-2026-10-19.md section 8.
naming: 3.1.2-usos17 = 3.1.2-usos16 (0001-0010, 0012, 0014-0021, byte for byte) + 0022 (USB disk service stage 2: runtime pool, port watch on the helper core, runtime bring-up and teardown of USB sticks, media check, record version 2; MEGASAS and UHCI off).
modified: MODIFIED version of CSMWrap 3.1.2 and of its SeaBIOS fork: quiet boot unless csmwrap.ini sets verbose = true (patches 0001-0003, as in 3.1.2-usos1), and SeaBIOS CSM boot priorities looked up in CSMWrap's BBS table by PCI address, USB mass storage included (patch 0004, 2026-09-29); the exact disk CSMWrap was loaded from becomes BIOS drive 0x80 also when other disks share its controller (patch 0005, 2026-10-11: CSMWrap tags its BBS entry with an FNV-1a hash of its sector 0, SeaBIOS moves the matching hard disk first, the others keep their order); and an ACPI 1.0 view for legacy systems on CSMWrap's RSDP copy (patch 0006, 2026-10-13: RsdtAddress 0 / invalid RSDT / RSDT without the FACP or APIC the XSDT lists -> a new RSDT from the XSDT entries below 4 GiB; FADT 32-bit FIRMWARE_CTRL/DSDT/PM/GPE fields 0 with the X_ field set below 4 GiB -> a FADT copy with them filled, referenced from the RSDT only; csmwrap.ini acpi_legacy_fadt = true (written only for Windows 2000 with ACPI) -> the RSDT FADT is always a copy cut to revision 1 / 116 bytes, because the 2000 ACPI HALs copy FADT.Length bytes into a 0x84-byte buffer; with the same option the RSDT's DSDT/SSDTs are copies whose static resource templates have QWord windows above 4 GiB cleared, because the 2000 acpi.sys truncates a QWord Length to 32 bits and stops with STOP 0xA5 (0x2) in its PCI root window check; a valid 1.0 view without the option is left untouched; logged as "USOS ACPI10"); and, only with the same csmwrap.ini acpi_legacy_fadt = true, a legacy-to-ACPI-mode transition as the last step before Legacy16Boot (patch 0007, 2026-10-14, diagnostic: RTC A/B read, FADT ACPI_ENABLE written to SMI_CMD when PM1a_CNT.SCI_EN is 0, SCI_EN polled for at most 3 s on the PM timer, RTC A/B read again; 8 result bytes at physical 0x4F4 (BDA inter-application communication area) for usosvid; logged as "USOS ACPIEN"); and APM power-off that works from every APM interface (patch 0008, 2026-10-15: 5307h BX=0001h CX=0003h first asks the helper core for UEFI ResetSystem(EfiResetShutdown) through the bios_proxy mailbox with a 2 s timeout - from real/V86 mode with %es = F000h, from the 32-bit protected-mode interface through %gs instead of the real-mode segment loads that faulted there - then writes ACPI S5 directly: SLP_TYPa/b read from Name(_S5) in the DSDT/SSDT (X470: 5 -> PM1a_CNT 0x3400; QEMU: 0), PM1a and PM1b, SLP_EN last; still on after 2 s with SCI_EN = 0: FADT ACPI_ENABLE to SMI_CMD and S5 again; still on: the call returns AH=60h instead of halting; the 16-bit PM interface goes straight to the S5 write; _PTS is not run; result bytes at BDA 4FCh-4FFh for INT 15h callers, logged as "USOS APMOFF"; SeaBIOS dprintf level 1 goes to csmwrap.ini serial_port when serial = true, through CsmwrapFlags bit 0x02 and the new CsmwrapSerialPort field; the SeaBIOS layout keeps at least 6144 bytes of F-segment allocation space, upstream minimum 2048, because the code no longer leaves free room in the F-segment; and a new APM power-off order with a record of every step (patch 0009, 2026-10-15, after Windows 98 SE on the X470 hung on its shutdown screen with usos7): 1. SCI_EN = 0 -> FADT ACPI_ENABLE to SMI_CMD, SCI_EN polled for at most 1 s; 2. PM1a_EVT and GPE0 status bits cleared, all their enables 0; 3. S5 (SLP_TYP from _S5, SLP_EN last), 2 s wait; 4. still on, INT 15h and 32-bit PM only: the helper-core UEFI ResetSystem (2 s timeout) as the last resort; 5. AH=60h; every wait bounded by the PM timer and a spin count; every step recorded in the CMOS RTC alarm bytes 01h/03h/05h as a valid alarm time (seconds 40 + step, minutes path * 15 + call count, hours 1 + APM function bitmap; armed 40/0/1 when CSMWrap starts SeaBIOS) because edk2 PcRtcInit resets an invalid alarm at every boot, and on port 80h as A0h | step; the USOS UEFI menu appends the record to EFI\USOS\Logs\apm-off.txt and writes 00:00:00 back; and SeaBIOS NVMe INT 13h that survives an OS driver stopping the controller (patch 0010, 2026-10-15, after Windows 98 SE on the X470 NVMe stopped at "It's now safe to turn off your computer": usosnvme.mpd rebuilds the admin queue in its own memory and sends CC.SHN + CC.EN = 0 on the exit to real mode, so WIN.COM /z could not be read for the APM power-off): before every read/write BAR 0 is read from PCI config space (a 64-bit BAR above 4 GiB is refused); a controller that is enabled, ready, not shutting down and runs SeaBIOS's admin queue is used as it is; enabled with another admin queue = a live OS driver, refused at once; otherwise memory + bus master on, CC = 0, the admin queue and I/O queue pair 1 cleared and re-created in the POST memory (no runtime allocation), logged as "USOS NVME"; writes after a re-arm carry FUA; and, only with csmwrap.ini acpi_legacy_fadt = true, a read-only diagnostic watcher on the hidden BIOS helper core (patch 0011, 2026-10-15, written by Codex and reviewed for USOS, after Windows 2000 SP4 with the ACPI HAL on the X470 stopped after kernel phase 1 with no heartbeat): FADT PM1a_EVT/PM1a_CNT/PM_TMR/GPE0 ports, TSC calibrated on the PM timer, one EfiReservedMemoryType page below 4 GiB that must be type 2 in the E820 map SeaBIOS gets, its address handed to the helper through a private trampoline dword and to BDA 4FCh-4FFh right before Legacy16Boot (the APM power-off record of patch 0008 uses the same bytes only at an INT 15h power-off, which the 2000 ACPI HAL never calls); the helper keeps serving the bios_proxy mailbox first, uses PAUSE + RDTSC instead of MWAIT and about once a second reads KeTickCount and KUSER_SHARED_DATA InterruptTime (physical addresses published by usosvid 1.3), PM1 STS/EN/CNT, GPE0 STS/EN and the PIC IMRs, and writes them to its page range 100h-1FFh and as one 80-column line on VGA text row 24; no port writes, no CMOS, IOAPIC or LAPIC access, logged as "USOS WATCH"); not in usos11: patch 0011 (the watcher) was dropped from the series; and, only with the same csmwrap.ini acpi_legacy_fadt = true, HPET and AMD GPIO devices hidden from Windows 2000 (patch 0012, 2026-10-17, after the X470 diagnosis found the 2000 SP4 acpi.sys page-faulting in its early boot IRQ arbitration for the HPET and, with that hidden, for the GPIO controller _SB.GPIO, IRQ 7): in the private DSDT/SSDT copies of patch 0006 a Device with a flat TermList (NameOp/MethodOp only), exactly one _HID and one _STA, whose _HID or a _CID entry is PNP0103, AMDI0030 or AMD0030 (string or EISA ID integer, _CID also as a Package), gets a _STA that returns 0 (Name -> Zero, method body -> Return (Zero) + Noop), in place, lengths and resources unchanged; dry run on the firmware table first (valid checksum only, a malformed PkgLength makes the whole table count 0), the copy must give the same result; firmware tables and the XSDT view unchanged; logged as "USOS W2KHIDE"); and, only with csmwrap.ini int13_boot_disk_only = true, only the disk CSMWrap was loaded from is a BIOS hard disk (patch 0014, 2026-10-18, see 3.1.2-usos11-int13x); and, only with csmwrap.ini pci_irq_routing = true (written by the Windows 9x flow only), PCI INTx routed to 8259 IRQs as a legacy BIOS POST does (patch 0015, 2026-10-18, after Windows Me on the X470 disabled the I211 and every other PCI device with an interrupt pin with Code 29 "the BIOS did not assign an IRQ": the firmware leaves LNKA..LNKH at IRQ 0 in PIC mode and 9x has no IRQ steering miniport for the AMD FCH): every PCI bus walked from the ACPI root bridges, each Interrupt Pin resolved through the PIC-mode _PRT (bridge swizzle for buses without one), used link devices keep a valid _CRS IRQ or get one from _PRS through _SRS (11, 10, 5, 9 first, least loaded, checked with _CRS; on failure the link is disabled with _DIS), Interrupt Line written, ELCR level bits set, and the $PIR built from that routing (every bus/device with a pin, one IRQ per pin); logged as "pciirq:"; and the USB mouse wheel through the BIOS pointing device (patch 0016, 2026-10-18, for USOSMOUS.DRV WM_MOUSEWHEEL on Windows 98/98 SE/Me and VBADOS VBMOUSE in DOS): usb_mouse_setup reads the HID report descriptor (zeroed buffer, at most 1024 bytes) and walks it (buttons 1-3, relative X/Y and wheel of the report that has X, report IDs, fields up to 16 bits, one Push level); with a wheel and every input report no longer than one interrupt packet the interface goes to the report protocol and that layout is decoded (other report IDs ignored, values clamped to +-127), otherwise the boot protocol as before; wMaxPacketSize up to 16; IntelliMouse emulation: sample rates 200, 100, 80 give device ID 3 when a wheel mouse is present, C204h returns the ID, C201h/C205h reset it; C205h package sizes 1-7 (3: the wheel in the handler Z word after the knock; 4-7: the 4th byte; 1/2: a byte stream); keyboards and the i8042 path unchanged; and the SeaBIOS options that only act on romfiles turned off (patch 0017, 2026-10-18: CONFIG_BOOTSPLASH, CONFIG_SERCON, CONFIG_HOST_BIOS_GEOMETRY; a CSM build has no romfile source, so the code never ran); and a USB mouse wheel diagnostics record (patch 0018, 2026-10-18, after Windows Me on the X470 with usos13 moved and clicked but had no wheel): usb_mouse_setup and handle_mouse write a VARLOW record (signature "USOS" "MWHL", version 1, 16-byte aligned, 312 bytes) with per mouse (first 4) interface, wMaxPacketSize, report/boot protocol and a reason code (hid_parse_mouse returns USB_MD_* codes instead of -1, same decisions), report ID, wDescriptorLength and the parsed layout, the first 160 bytes of the first mouse report descriptor, the IntelliMouse ID and last two sample rates, packet / wheel packet / skipped packet counters and the last raw packet, for USOSDBG.EXE; never read back by the BIOS; and more mouse shapes for the wheel (patch 0019, 2026-10-18, generic, no vendor or product IDs): with report IDs, input reports of other IDs longer than one packet are skipped by packet count (up to 4 IDs, 127 packets; after a report that fills its last packet exactly, a byte-identical next packet of the same mouse is taken as the zero-length end and skipped), descriptors up to 4096 bytes, up to 16 input report IDs; usb.c sets up the first later boot mouse interface (alternate setting 0) of a device whose first boot HID interface is a keyboard, with a copy of the device record; keyboards unchanged, no second keyboard; and the USB mouse wheel in the handler Z word without the knock plus an INT 15h C2xxh call ring (patch 0020, 2026-10-19, after Windows Me on the X470 with usos14 showed the wheel field decoded and wheel packets arriving but the emulated device ID back at 0 with sample rates 10, 40 after USOSMOUS.DRV's knock: with 3-byte packages the wheel value always goes in the far-call handler's Z word, with or without device ID 3 (a standard handler ignores Z; z is 0 for a mouse without a wheel); package sizes 1/2 and 4-7 unchanged; the USOSMWHL record (version byte still 1, first 310 bytes unchanged) gets at +312 magic "C2RG", a call counter, the next slot and 16 entries of 12 bytes: AX, BX, ES on entry, the caller CS:IP, the emulated device ID after the call and the result (0, or 80h | AH with CF set); written only, never read back); and a USB disk service for an OS driver (patch 0021, 2026-10-19, for USOSUSB.MPD, the Windows 95/98/98 SE/Me SCSIPORT miniport of USOS: SeaBIOS stays the only xHCI owner; the CSMPPrxy mailbox is 64-byte aligned and carries channel 1 at +48 (magic UDS1, req_phys, doorbell, done) in the same cache line, the helper loop serves channel 0 first and then calls usos_uds_service when doorbell != done; the request block is read once from the OS physical address and validated (magic, version, size, op, device, LUN, CDB length 6-16, direction, at most 64 KiB, no wrap, nothing in A0000h-FFFFFh); ops ENUM (device table of up to 8 xHCI BOT devices, registered at setup), SCSI (CBW / data / CSW with any CDB and direction, automatic REQUEST SENSE), RESET (BOT reset recovery: Bulk-Only Mass Storage Reset, CLEAR_FEATURE(ENDPOINT_HALT) and xHCI Reset Endpoint / Stop Endpoint / Set TR Dequeue Pointer on both bulk endpoints), EJECT, STATUS; a device with a BIOS drive number is refused (OWNED); own bulk TDs to physical buffers, two chained TRBs with ISP across a 64 KiB boundary, controller (capability dword, halted, host system error) and root-port CCS checked on every wait pass so an unplug ends the request at once (GONE) and the slot gets Disable Slot; the device control pipe is kept for the reset recovery; VID:PID, INQUIRY strings and READ CAPACITY of LUN 0 read on the helper at the first request for a device without a BIOS number, so POST sends nothing new; no PCI configuration access from the helper core; a VARLOW record USOS UDSK version 1, 768 bytes: per device state, counters and last CDB / CSW / sense, the BIOS hard disks and CD-ROMs as mapped, a ring of the last 16 events; written only, for USOSDBG.EXE / USOSLOG.EXE; and USB stick hot-swap for the USB disk service (patch 0022, 2026-10-19, only with csmwrap.ini int13_boot_disk_only = true: a 12 KiB pool from ZoneHigh at POST, every xHCI registered and kept running without devices, a port watch on the helper core about every 100 ms once an OS client used channel 1 (root-port CCS plus a latch of CSC set in xhci_process_events), runtime bring-up of a bulk-only stick (port reset, Enable Slot, Address Device, descriptors, SET_CONFIGURATION, Configure Endpoint, GET MAX LUN; then INQUIRY, READ CAPACITY and a media check), teardown on unplug (Disable Slot, chunk freed), device table entries re-used with a new generation, a connected port without a device slot (POST did not set it up) brought up the same way, EJECT disables the slot; the helper loop spins with PAUSE instead of MWAIT once the watch is armed; every boot: the media check (MBR types, FAT12/16/32 / NTFS / exFAT / GPT) and exact KiB counters; the USOSUDSK record becomes version 2, 984 bytes; seabios-config without CONFIG_MEGASAS and CONFIG_USB_UHCI for ROM room))

source_archive.note: unpatched 3.1.2 tree with all submodules and seabios/.version (shared with 3.1.2-usos1); the usos17 source is this archive plus patches/*.patch applied in order with patch -p1

embedded_blobs_note: hashes of the build outputs Csm16-usos1.bin / vgabios-usos1.bin of the VM run (and its in-guest repeat build)

upstream_rebuild.note: the same source and toolchain built WITHOUT patches in each run: matches 3.1.2-usos1/manifest.json upstream_rebuild

build: python tools/csmwrap_build/run_build_vm.py --work <dir> --accel whpx --patches tools/vendor/csmwrap/3.1.2-usos17/patches --usos-version 3.1.2-usos17 (pinned toolchain, lock.json); one VM run on 2026-10-19 with its in-guest repeat build gave the same binary, the unpatched build matches upstream_rebuild
tests: tools/tests/csmwrap/test_csmwrap_uds17.py (series, layouts of usb-uds.h = usosuds.h version 2, request check, wiring); tools/tests/csmwrap/run_csmwrap_uds_qemu.py (QEMU q35 + OVMF, usb-kbd + usb-mouse + usb-storage on qemu-xhci: stage 1 steps, then keyboard, hot-plug, fast replug, EJECT, 6 unplug/replug cycles, keyboard, the version 2 record checked; owned mode); the usos16 QEMU regressions (see docs/research/csmwrap.md section 23)
layout: SeaBIOS: ROM 125504 of 131072 bytes (95.8 %, 5568 free; usos16 126656, 4416 free; MEGASAS and UHCI off, 0022 code on); 16-bit 34624, 32-bit segmented 4118, 32-bit flat 36458 (usos16 33386), flat init 39392, low memory 3968 (usos16 3472; the record 984, the watch state 264), F-segment variables 3840 (usos16 3744)
